newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed well ahead on Thursday, benefiting from a worldwide assets rally after benign U.S. employment data in the afternoon.

Guilders had shown little inclination to trade before the data and dealers said that despite the sharp price spike afterwards, turnover had not been similarly stimulated and there was still a shortage of buyers.
"Even at good prices it can be really hard to get rid of paper," one said.
The data showed U.S. payroll growth had been moderate in May and June.
A jump in the unemployment rate in June to 5.0 percent also soothed fears of a tight labour market and an August rate hike.

The long end of the Guilder curve was the main beneficiary, rebounding after some days of being sold against the ten-year area. Dealers said the flattening was timely, as the long bond had begun to look cheap.
Guilders extended Wednesday's spread gains against Bunds in the five-year area, but underperformed further out on the curve.
With the U.S. closed, the Dutch market was seen idling for the rest of the week, possibly set for a longer quiet period.
